description.p: A controller-first mod manager for Steam and Heroic games on SteamOS handhelds.
What a mod needs, lined up, and Cyberpunk's frameworks working under Proton:

ul.li: After an add, one sheet says what the mod needs; Get them all gets the whole chain in turn, with the next Nexus page opening by itself on its Slow download button, Skip and Stop, and a row in My mods to go on later
Before you play warns when a mod that is on misses what it needs, with Get what they need first
My mods keeps what other mods need under one collapsed Dependencies row; X options move a mod in or out, and the load order stays as it is
Cyberpunk 2077: when RED4ext or Cyber Engine Tweaks would stop with error 998, Before you play installs Microsoft's Visual C++ runtime into the game's Proton setup in one press
The first-run tutorial matches how Turbine works now, with a fifth card on what it sets up for you

description.p: Updates that check without being refused, and keys and a mouse the way PC players expect:

ul.li: Check for updates no longer runs into GitHub's hourly limit, looks at most once every 6 hours at a start, and says so plainly when GitHub asks it to wait
Turbine's own icon on its window in Desktop Mode's taskbar, and the menu's icon is read again after an update
Keyboard: W A S D or the arrows, Enter or Space, Esc (Settings on a game's first page), Q and E for the pages, F to find, R for options, hold Tab for the quick wheel, hold Space for 3 seconds to play
Mouse: a double-click opens a mod, the side buttons go back and to the next page, and the bar shows named buttons with no key caps
An older Seamless Co-op file left without an answer is settled when another arrives or Turbine closes

description.p: Start, pages, keys and a safer way into Steam:

ul.li: Start opens Settings; hold it for 3 seconds to play (A on Play still plays)
Get mods is a page of its own: My mods to the left, Load order to the right
The quick wheel's middle picks nothing and closes it
Keyboard and mouse work everywhere, and the hints follow what you used last
Smoother animations, with Full, Reduced or Off in Settings, Look
Elden Ring and other me3 games: the game's tamper protection is switched off for modded play, which should stop it closing by itself soon after it starts
A Steam tool, Turbine (mods), picked once in the game's Properties, in place of restarting Steam in Game Mode
Seamless Co-op: never starts without a session password, one copy per game, and its screens say it loads only with Play Seamless Co-op
The Co-op tile is asked about once and added in Desktop Mode
A game that started and closed says so, with the Proton it ran on, instead of "didn't start"
One Nexus sign-in status everywhere, and better matching of games to Nexus
A new icon: the brass mark on a clear background
A quieter activity log, fuller bug reports, and one Downloads folder everywhere
Y always opens Find; R3 runs Undo while a message shows
Edit settings: X opens Options (show as text or a list, reset to default)
Steam setup picks the account signed in last, and a restart is only offered when it is really needed
Updates install where Turbine was installed; downloads are caught from your real Downloads folder
Turbine looks for the controller again in Desktop Mode, and says what to do if it can't see one
Sign in keeps one waiting session; a busy Turbine answers the Steam menu plainly

description.p: Easier, clearer and checked on every screen:

ul.li: Elden Ring and other me3 games start with mods from Steam's Play; Turbine can set up Steam for you with one restart
Seamless Co-op chosen at Play, its settings one press away, and an optional Co-op tile in the Steam library
Taps never go through pop-ups; A selects and B goes back everywhere
Search, sort and categories take effect at once and always show the results
Simple mod names with the Nexus picture, and Edit settings right on the mod
Sign in to Nexus through Chrome that tells you what is happening
Plain errors with a next step, Steam library art, and a start-up animation
Optional Steam menu plugin (Decky)

description.p: Modded launches through Steam, Edit settings and a roomier bar:

ul.li: Elden Ring and other me3 games start with mods from Steam's own Play, so Game Mode shows them; a one-time Launch Options line, with Undo
Seamless Co-op button beside Play, with a settings page
Edit settings for any mod or game config file, with controller-friendly controls
Launch check, Report a problem, game update warning, and separate normal, modded and co-op saves
Interface size from 50% to 150% with real buttons; a taller, spaced-out bottom bar; Activity log opens again

description.p: Full screen mods and anti-cheat games:

ul.li: No top bar: the game, its status and Play live in the bottom bar; scrolling down goes full screen
Y opens one pop-up for search, sort and categories
Elden Ring, Nightreign, Armored Core VI, Dark Souls III and Sekiro run mods offline through me3, without changing the game folder
Seamless Co-op through me3; a guide for Halo's own anti-cheat switch; online-only anti-cheat games never get mods
Saves go back even when the save folder was deleted

description.p: Mods for any game, and a roomier, cleaner Turbine:

ul.li: Basic support for every Steam and Heroic game, asking where files go when it isn't sure
The header slides away while you scroll; a details panel for the selected mod
Get mods shows 4 cards per row with a short summary
The quick wheel is a pie: point at a wedge to pick it
Clean mod names, Rename, and Open its Nexus page
Save backups before Play, Why won't it start, Check game folder, press or hold, reduce motion
Nexus opens full screen inside Turbine, driven by the controller and pointer; sign-in is remembered
Press Slow download and the mod lands in Game Mods and is added, with Play ready
Mod Manager Download always asks first, so nothing downloads without your say
Sign in with Google through your own browser when the browser helper is paired
More game art, from your own Steam art and Steam's newer covers

description.p: New controls and an easier start:

ul.li: One selection and one meaning per button; the quick wheel on View; the right stick pointer with RT and R3 as the left click
A short beginner tutorial on first run, replayable from Settings, Help
Fewer steps from a game to a mod in it; clicking any row does what A does
Game Mode opens Chrome through Steam, with Steam's browser one press away
The browser helper updates itself; a clear prompt to press Slow download on Nexus
Holds such as Delete for good only count while a button is really held
Settings, Labs, Activity log with Copy to clipboard
Game Mode opens Chrome through Steam, and the browser helper opens the Nexus page in a new tab
A one-time guide to add Chrome to Steam, with Steam's browser as a fallback
Nexus API key help: where to find it, one-press Paste, and what a free key does
Menus and sheets fit and scroll on every screen size

description.p: Round three, from the game testers:

ul.li: A runs the highlighted button everywhere, and the controls legend matches each screen
SKSE can be installed from the mod menu, the game menu and the check before Play
Trending works in Get mods; Sort and Category open as lists; B keeps your place
Interface size ends at the largest size that fits
Kingdom Come: warnings for mods made for the other game, and Put back my mod_order.txt
Loadouts, and Go back to an earlier setup
Keyboard and mouse hints in Desktop Mode
Mod pages load from Nexus without errors, and one failing part never hides the page
Kingdom Come: Deliverance and Kingdom Come: Deliverance II
A prompt when a modded game closes early, with a way back to the setup that worked
Which mod wins when two change the same file, and a way to choose
Requirements both ways, with a guided list of what is still missing
Find, Show and Sort on My mods, and updates without a key
Play without the script extender

description.p: Getting mods made easy, and a new layout:

ul.li: Browse, search and sort a game's Nexus mods inside Turbine, no key needed
One press gets a mod; the browser helper saves Nexus downloads into Game Mods with no Save box
Nexus opens in Game Mode, with Steam's browser as a fallback
New layout with My mods, Get mods and Load order, plain words throughout
Interface size slider, TV layout only with an external display, and every size change can be undone
Fuller controller support: B goes back everywhere, Find, hold Start for Play options, faster lists, back grips
Recently removed mods can be deleted for good
Mods downloaded in any browser are found in Downloads with no setup, even while Turbine was closed
Controller pointer: right stick moves it, RT clicks, LT right clicks, turning the left stick scrolls
Mod Manager Download without a Nexus key explains how to use Slow download instead
The browser helper is optional

description.p: Nexus downloads through your own browser, for testing on the owner's handhelds:

ul.li: Downloads from Nexus Mods in your browser are added to the right game
A status card shows over the browser in Desktop Mode and over other apps in Game Mode
Browser helper for Chrome, Brave, Edge, Chromium and Vivaldi shows installer choices on the Nexus page
A warning with install steps when no browser is found
Cyberpunk 2077 and The Witcher 3 checks before Play, and Proton settings for every game

description.p: Mods you can use, for testing on the owner's handhelds:

ul.li: Add mods from zip files in Downloads, turn them on and off, and set their order where it matters
Recently removed keeps uninstalled mods for 7 days, with Undo
Changes go into the game a few seconds after the last edit and when leaving Turbine
Play checks the game first: game updates, missing mod loaders, low space and exFAT drives
Game menu with Play original and Restore last working setup
Rules for Skyrim Special Edition, Cyberpunk 2077, The Witcher 3, Stardew Valley, Valheim, Lethal Company and Risk of Rain 2
BepInEx games under Proton get the winhttp setting they need, with a backup of the old settings
